HOME AND DAILY LIFE LESSON · HOME AND DAILY LIFE · AGES 3–5 YEARS

Storage Words — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches storage as a home-for-everything: five words, five real homes in your house, and a game that turns tidy-up time into sending things back where they live.

What is this?

Storage is where things live when they are not being used: socks in the drawer, dishes in the cupboard, books on the shelf, toys in the basket, surprises in the box.

What does it mean?

Tidy-up time fails when putting away has no address. Once each thing has a named home, the child is not cleaning — the child is rehoming, which is a completely different feeling.

What does the child need to know?

You need the card and five real storage homes your own house uses. Match the card where you can; the box can be any box — it is the most flexible member.

Why this matters

The word cupboard wears its passport openly: UK homes say cupboard, US homes say cabinet or closet. Say yours, offer the other, and the storage map works in both countries.

What it teaches

Organization logic (a place for everything), matching (thing to home), and the tidy-up identity — I am the person who sends things home.

Words to learn

drawercupboardcabinetshelfbasketboxstorage

Say this to your child

“"Storage words! Everything in this house lives somewhere. The spoon lives in the drawer, the teddy lives in the basket — let us send everybody home."”

Step by step

  1. Show the card: "five homes — let us meet the real ones in our house."
  2. Open the drawer together: one thing in, one thing out, say its address — "the drawer."
  3. Cupboard or cabinet: the dishes live here; open, look, close gently.
  4. Shelf and basket: one book home, one toy home, said out loud.
  5. The box last — "the box is the most generous home, it takes anything" — and tidy-up begins.

Look closer at the picture

On this card the words "Storage Words" sit over an open drawer, a two-door cupboard, a three-tier shelf, a woven basket with handles and a lidded box.

Ask your child

"Where does the spoon live?" "Where does the teddy live?" "Which storage home takes anything at all?" (the box)

What your child can say or do

Your child might give every object an address all day — "sock, drawer!" — invent homes for things that lack them, or close every drawer in the house like a little landlord.

Out in the real world

Storage runs the whole world: the shop has shelves, the library has shelves, the car has a glove box. A child who knows storage words reads rooms everywhere.

Try it together

Send It Home: five things on the rug, five homes named. The child carries each one to its address — the last delivery gets a cheer. Pack away time is now the game, not the argument.

Understanding check

Ask: "Where do the dishes live?" (the cupboard — the cabinet) "Where do the toys live?" (the basket) "What is the word for where things live?" (storage)

This lesson pairs with the Storage Words flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Home and Daily Life.
